analysis:
This batch contains only documentation and a changelog entry (changelog.d/provider-prompt-token-reuse.md, docs/architecture/components/provider.md lines 75-83, docs/architecture/inference.md head lines 790-806). No executable code is visible, so the implementation of the described behavior is unverified.

The docs describe three behavior changes whose source was not supplied:
1. PromptTokenCache reuses token IDs for chat-template pieces within one prefix-cache scope. The docs state reuse never crosses a scope, with load-time self-check and sampled background comparisons as safeguards. This touches T-041, since token-piece caching is a new in-memory cross-request state. Open questions: whether the cache key includes the coordinator-authored cacheSalt, and whether timing differences (5-8 ms hit vs 102-264 ms miss) add a TTFT oracle. Any such oracle would be narrower than the accepted SEC-035 same-account oracle if the scope is the authenticated account scope. Also unverified: whether the cache is bounded in size and TTL, and whether plaintext-derived data persists to disk.
2. ChatTemplateLoopRewrites renders Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS templates through rewritten loops. A rewrite that deviates from the served template could change the prompt the model sees. The docs claim load-time and sampled comparisons, but a sampled check is not exhaustive.
3. Cold-load work-queue release (ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift) lets later requests, cancels and attestation challenges proceed during a model load. This improves availability for T-010 and the App Attest challenge handling. The cancel-on-admission-return semantics, the ordering against grant revocation (T-053), and connection-invalidation handling cannot be verified without the code. The docs say connection, drain and model-management events still wait.

The DARKBLOOM_TTFT_* env toggles are provider env knobs. Whether they are in passthroughEnvKeys is not shown, and they are operator-controlled, so they are not an adversary-reachable surface for consumers.

No findings from docs alone. The Swift implementation (PromptTokenCache.swift, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites, ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift) should get a deeper review if it appears in another batch.
